title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet

epigraph.quote: Revenue is a vanity metric in process manufacturing; cash conversion and return on incremental capital over a full cycle tell the truth.
epigraph.author: Forensic Accounting Principle

web_blocks.html: A ten-year forensic audit reveals an exceptional balance-sheet transformation at Tanfac [6]. The period spans FY15 through September 2026 [6]. A major capital-raising program punctuated this progression in 2026 [6]. Revenue compounded at a 22.4% ten-year median growth rate [6]. Top line expanded from ₹120 crore in FY15 to ₹711 crore in FY26 [6]. Trailing twelve-month revenue reached ₹784 crore through September 2026 [6]. However, operating profitability has remained distinctly cyclical throughout this decade [6]. Operating margins swung from 7% in FY15 to 24% in FY19 [6]. Margins dipped to 16% in FY20 before rebounding to 24% in FY22 and FY25 [6]. Profitability then normalized to 16% in FY26 and 14% on a trailing basis [6].

web_blocks.caption: TANFACIND: 10-Year Profit & Loss Trajectory (FY18–FY26 & TTM)
web_blocks.takeaway: Sales expanded 4.4x from ₹162 Cr (FY18) to ₹711 Cr (FY26), while FY26 PAT dipped 20% YoY to ₹70 Cr as gross margin normalized and depreciation rose 70% to ₹17 Cr [6][20].

web_blocks.html: Cash Conversion Forensics (CFO versus PAT and EBITDA): Between FY15 and FY21, Tanfac demonstrated textbook cash generation [6]. Cumulative operating cash flow of ₹174 crore comfortably exceeded cumulative net profit of ₹65 crore [6]. This strong cash conversion enabled total debt elimination by March 2020 [6]. From FY22 through FY24, CFO-to-EBITDA conversion remained healthy between 73% and 82% [6]. Cumulative operating cash flow was ₹121 crore against ₹161 crore of net profit [6]. However, cash conversion slowed during FY25 and FY26 as top-line growth accelerated [6]. CFO-to-EBITDA conversion fell to 47% in FY25, generating ₹33 crore cash flow against ₹88 crore profit [6]. Conversion reached 56% in FY26, with ₹43 crore cash flow against ₹70 crore profit [6]. Working capital absorption drove this slowdown [6]. Larger inventory and receivables supported ₹711 crore of annual scale [6]. In addition, Days Payable compressed from 77 days in FY24 to 48 days in FY25 and 21 days in FY26 [6]. Simultaneously, heavy capital expenditures turned Free Cash Flow negative [6]. Free Cash Flow was -₹2 crore in FY24, -₹64 crore in FY25, and -₹39 crore in FY26 [6].

web_blocks.caption: TANFACIND: 10-Year Cash Flow & Free Cash Flow Profile (FY17–FY26)
web_blocks.takeaway: CFO/EBITDA conversion compressed from 73%–121% (FY17–FY24) to 47%–56% (FY25–FY26), turning FCF negative (-₹105 Cr cumulative across FY24–FY26) during the capex buildout [6].

web_blocks.html: Balance Sheet & Credit Fortification: Tanfac operated without debt from FY20 through FY24 [6]. It then added term borrowings to fund plant expansions [6]. Debt rose to ₹41 crore in FY25, ₹93 crore in FY26, and ₹136 crore by September 2026 [6]. Crucially, a ₹349.41 crore equity raise restructured the balance sheet in mid-2026 [6][17][19]. Tanfac completed a ₹250 crore QIP in June and a ₹99.41 crore preferential issue in September [17][19]. Reserves expanded from ₹363 crore in March 2026 to ₹726 crore in September 2026 [6]. Total net worth reached ₹737 crore, keeping debt-to-equity conservative at approximately 0.18 times [6]. Capital work-in-progress increased from ₹29 crore in March 2026 to ₹153 crore in September 2026 [6]. That increase reflected active construction on the HFC-32 project [6][11]. ICRA upgraded Tanfac to [ICRA]A+ Stable and [ICRA]A1+ in April 2025 [12][31]. The rating agency reaffirmed these marks in October 2026 across enhanced bank facilities of ₹225 crore [12][31].

web_blocks.caption: TANFACIND: Balance Sheet Transformation (Mar 2018–Sep 2026)
web_blocks.takeaway: Net worth expanded from ₹13 Cr (Mar 2018) to ₹737 Cr (Sep 2026) via retained earnings and the 2026 QIP/preferential raise, keeping borrowings modest at ₹136 Cr against ₹153 Cr CWIP [6].

web_blocks.caption: TANFACIND: Working Capital Days & Return on Capital Employed (FY17–FY26)
web_blocks.takeaway: ROCE peaked at 78% (FY19) and 67% (FY22) before moderating to 24% in FY26 as heavy fixed-asset additions expanded the capital base [6].

web_blocks.html: ROCE/ROE & Capital Efficiency: Return on Capital Employed averaged above 40% during the debt-free upcycle [6]. ROCE registered 67% in FY22, 48% in FY23, 33% in FY24, and 42% in FY25 [6]. The metric then moderated to 23.9% in FY26, with Return on Equity at 20.3% [6]. Rapid asset expansion drove this moderation [6]. Gross fixed assets rose from ₹61 crore in FY24 to ₹212 crore in FY26 and ₹237 crore by September 2026 [6]. With ₹737 crore of equity now recorded, Tanfac enters a capital deployment test [6]. Sustaining returns above 20% requires commissioning the ₹495 crore HFC-32 project cleanly [11][12]. Management must also restore operating margins above 16% [8][20].

book_subsections.title: Ten Years of Numbers: Growth Without Linear Margins
paragraphs: When you and I open Tanfac's ten-year financial ledger, two truths jump off the page. First, the top-line growth has been remarkable: sales compounded from ₹120 crore in FY15 to ₹711 crore in FY26, and reached ₹784 crore on a trailing twelve-month basis through September 2026. Second, profitability has never moved in a straight line. Operating margins hit 24 percent in FY19, dropped to 16 percent in FY20, surged back to 24 percent in FY22 and FY25, and slipped back to 16 percent in FY26.

Now look at cash conversion, because that is where forensic discipline pays off. From FY15 through FY24, Tanfac converted operating profit into real cash reliably—often 73 to 121 percent of EBITDA. In FY25 and FY26, that conversion dropped to 47 percent and 56 percent. Why? Not because customers stopped paying—Debtor Days actually improved from 65 to 57—but because Tanfac paid its own suppliers much faster, shrinking Days Payable from 48 days to 21 days while funding larger inventories. Add ₹82 crore of FY26 capex on top of ₹43 crore of operating cash flow, and free cash flow stayed negative at ₹39 crore.

book_subsections.title: The Post-QIP Fortress and the Return-on-Capital Test
paragraphs: That negative free cash flow explains why the 2026 equity raises were so decisive. After running completely debt-free from FY20 to FY24, borrowings edged up to ₹93 crore in FY26 and ₹136 crore by September 2026. By raising ₹250 crore in the June 2026 QIP and ₹99.41 crore in the September 2026 preferential issue, management pushed net worth to ₹737 crore, giving Tanfac a low 0.18x debt-to-equity ratio and an ICRA A-plus stable credit rating even with ₹153 crore sitting in capital work-in-progress.

Here is the catch you and I must keep front of mind: a bigger equity base raises the bar for capital efficiency. Tanfac's ROCE sat at 42 percent in FY25 when equity was ₹312 crore, and moderated to 23.9 percent in FY26. With ₹737 crore of net worth now deployed, earning a 20-plus percent return on capital over the next three years depends squarely on commissioning the HFC-32 plant on schedule and restoring operating spreads above the 12 percent trough seen in Q2 FY27.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: A fortress balance sheet removes bankruptcy risk during a capex cycle, but it does not guarantee high returns on incremental equity. Watch two forensic ratios over the next four quarters: whether Days Payable normalizes to lift CFO/EBITDA back above 70%, and whether asset turns on the ₹237 Cr fixed-asset base + ₹153 Cr CWIP hold above 2.0x.

book_paragraphs: Chapter 6 is where we put the financial statements under a forensic microscope across a full ten-year window. Between FY17 and FY26, Tanfac's revenue compounded from roughly ₹140 crore to ₹711.07 crore, while operating profit climbed from low-single-digit crores to ₹114 crore in FY26 (and ₹130+ crore at the FY25 peak). Return on capital employed averaged a healthy 23.9% and three-year ROE reached 25.1%, demonstrating that once Aluminium Fluoride losses were behind it, the core HF complex could generate attractive returns on invested capital.

However, the cash-flow forensics tell a more nuanced story than the income statement alone. In FY25 and FY26, cumulative EBITDA exceeded ₹200 crore, yet cash flow from operations lagged at 47% to 56% of EBITDA. In FY26 specifically, ₹114 crore of EBITDA produced only ₹43 crore of operating cash flow—primarily because trade payables shrank from 48 days to 21 days as the company paid suppliers faster while scaling inventories and receivables for the expanded plant. After ₹82 crore of capital expenditure, free cash flow was negative ₹39 crore.

The balance sheet today is undeniably strong thanks to the ₹349.41 crore equity raise across the June 2026 QIP and September 2026 preferential issue, lifting net worth to roughly ₹737 crore and keeping debt-to-equity conservative at 0.18x with an [ICRA]A+ (Stable) rating. That liquidity buffer removes bankruptcy or debt-distress risk during the ₹495 crore HFC-32 buildout. Still, dilution is real, and until free cash flow turns sustainably positive post-capex, investors are funding growth upfront.

Let us double-check one more forensic detail in the ten-year accounts: equity dilution and capital intensity. Before 2026, Tanfac's equity base barely budged for decades—around 99.75 lakh shares (pre-split ₹10 face value), later split 1:2 in March 2026 to ₹5 face value (~1.995 crore shares). Then, in June and September 2026, the QIP and preferential issue added fresh shares to raise ₹349.41 crore, lifting total diluted shares toward 2.163 crore and book value to ₹341 per share.

Raising equity at ₹1,965.83 per share was smart corporate finance for existing shareholders, because issuing stock at a high multiple funds ₹495 crore of capex without burdening the balance sheet with debt. However, it also raises the denominator: future net profit must now be divided across a larger share count, and the new HFC-32 assets must earn well above the cost of equity just to maintain Tanfac's historical 23.9% ROCE.

In financial forensics, never confuse a healthy balance sheet with high cash-conversion quality. Tanfac's balance sheet after the ₹349.41 crore equity raise is rock solid—low 0.18x debt-to-equity, ₹737 crore net worth, and an [ICRA]A+ rating. Yet the cash flow statement reminds us that operating cash flow in FY26 was ₹43 crore against ₹114 crore of EBITDA, leaving free cash flow at negative ₹39 crore after ₹82 crore of capex. Until working capital normalizes and the new plants throw off surplus cash, the equity story relies on future returns on capital rather than current free cash yield.

Another key forensic checkpoint is return on incremental capital employed. Between FY22 and FY25, Tanfac earned exceptional returns because it sweat existing Cuddalore infrastructure and debottlenecked AHF. Now, with ₹349.41 crore of fresh equity and a ₹495 crore HFC-32 project ahead, the capital base has more than doubled to ₹737 crore of net worth. Maintaining a 20%+ ROCE on that enlarged equity and asset base requires generating well over ₹150 crore of annual EBIT once HFC-32 ramps.
